titleEn: Law Adopting the Protocol 5 of ASEAN on Obligation of Insurance Vehicle

articles.en:
Definitions. For the purposes of this Protocol, the following terms shall have the meanings set out below: a. "National Bureau" means the agency duly appointed by each Contracting Party to carry out the functions necessary for the operation of the ASEAN Scheme on Compulsory Motor Vehicle Insurance as provided for in this Protocol.
b. "Insurer" means an insurance company which is a member of any one of the National Bureaux.
c. "Bureau Council" means the body established by the representatives of all National Bureaux as provided for in Article 11 of this Protocol. d. "Blue Card" means a certificate identifying the holder which evidences a policy of compulsory motor vehicle insurance issued by the National Bureau of a Contracting Party in accordance with the terms of this Protocol.
e. "Transit vehicle for inland transport" means a type of vehicle used to carry goods in transit through the territory of one or more Contracting Parties, where such transit is effected with or without transhipment, and where the loading, unloading or change in the mode of carriage constitutes only part of the entire journey, which begins or ends outside the frontier of one or more Contracting Parties through which the vehicle travels, as described in the insurance certificate or on the Blue Card.
f. "Insurance certificate" means a document of contract issued by an Insurer to an insured person covering death or bodily injury and/or damage to property caused by the use of a transit vehicle on the road.
g. "Holder of the insurance certificate" means the legal or natural person who holds a policy of compulsory motor vehicle insurance, or any person who lawfully holds a Blue Card.
h. "Road accident" means an event or unexpected occurrence arising in connection with a transit vehicle on the road and causing death, bodily injury and/or damage to property.
i. "Transit transport operator" means the owner, the driver and/or the agent of a transit vehicle on the road who (1) is duly authorised by his own country, or holds a licence, to provide transport services, and holds documents certifying compliance with the rules and regulations set out in such authorisation or licence, and (2) is duly registered as a transit transport operator by the National Transit Transport Coordinating Committee of his respective country. [Legacy-font text in source: not convertible to Unicode]

Implementation. Pursuant to Article 3 and paragraph 3 of Article 14 of the Framework Agreement, the Contracting Parties hereby agree to implement all the provisions of this Protocol on the establishment of the ASEAN Scheme on Compulsory Motor Vehicle Insurance, so that transit transport operators and transit vehicles on the road of any Contracting Party may be adequately insured in respect of death, bodily injury and/or damage
to property caused by road accidents in the territory of other Contracting Parties.

Scope of the obligation of compulsory motor vehicle insurance. The ASEAN Scheme on Compulsory Motor Vehicle Insurance as established in this Protocol shall at least provide the minimum requirements prescribed by the laws and regulations governing the obligation of motor vehicle insurance in force in a country or in countries of transit and at the place of destination.

Obligations of the Contracting Parties. In addition to the obligations stipulated in the provisions of this Protocol, the Contracting Parties shall endeavour to take the measures necessary for the implementation of this Protocol, and in particular:
a. to arrange for one or more insurance companies established in their territory and providing motor vehicle insurance to adopt the Blue Card scheme as described in this Protocol; b. to arrange for the adoption of the laws and regulations that may be required for the implementation of this Protocol; c. to arrange to ensure that their National Bureau has sufficient funds to discharge its obligations as provided for in Article 10 of this Protocol.

Requirement to hold a Blue Card. Transit vehicles on the road shall carry a valid Blue Card, to be produced upon request.
Issue of the Blue Card. The Blue Card shall be issued by the National Bureau of each Contracting Party in accordance with Article 10 of this Protocol. Scope and validity of the Blue Card
1. Throughout its period of validity, the Blue Card shall serve as evidence of the existence of a policy of compulsory motor vehicle insurance as described in Article 3 of this Protocol. b. The Blue Card shall be valid for a specified period, not exceeding one year, irrespective of the number of transit journeys.
c. The Blue Card shall be valid for one particular transit vehicle on the road and shall not be transferable in any circumstances whatsoever.
Article 8. Particulars and form of the Blue Card
1. The Blue Card shall set out the following particulars:
a. the name and address of the National Bureau issuing the Card; b. the country in which the insurance certificate is valid; c. the name and address of the insurance company; d. the identification of the transit vehicle on the road; e. the name and address of the holder of the insurance certificate; f. the date of issue of the Card and the date of its expiry; g. the name and address of the National Bureau in each Contracting Party; h. the serial number of the Card; and i. the signature and seal of the National Bureau issuing the Card. 2. The format, terms, size and layout of the Blue Card shall be determined by the Bureau Council. The Card shall be printed in the English language. Establishment of the National Bureau
1. Each Contracting Party shall establish a National Bureau having the functions set out in Article 10 of this Protocol.
2. The National Bureau shall be established by the insurance companies licensed to underwrite motor vehicle insurance.
Article 10. Functions of the National Bureau. The National Bureau shall perform the following functions: a. to issue Blue Cards to transit transport operators in its own country after verifying that such operator holds a motor vehicle insurance policy meeting the requirements of the compulsory motor vehicle insurance of that country.
b. to sell the national motor vehicle insurance policy which provides compulsory insurance cover at least
at the minimum level to transit transport operators of other countries entering that country.
c. to stamp the Blue Card after verifying that the transit transport operator of another country has purchased the motor vehicle insurance policy required, in response to the demand of the compulsory motor vehicle insurance of that country.
d. upon being informed of a road accident occurring in its territory and caused by the holder of such Blue Card, to verify the circumstances of the accident and, on the basis of its own investigation, to take the necessary measures. In that event, the National Bureau shall provide information to the insurance company concerned in settling the claim on behalf of that insurance company.
e. to obtain the prior consent of the insurance company concerned before settling any claim. f. to contact the insurance company concerned in order to recover the sums already paid out as compensation.
Article 11. Establishment of the Bureau Council. The Bureau Council shall be established to coordinate and supervise the financial, administrative, technical and legal operations of the National Bureaux of the countries of the Contracting Parties.
Article 14. Institutional arrangements
1. The ASEAN Insurance Regulators Meeting shall be responsible for reviewing the coordination and supervision of all aspects relating to the effective implementation of this Protocol.
b. The ASEAN Secretariat shall submit regular reports on the progress of the implementation of this Protocol to the Transit Transport Coordinating Board established in accordance with Article 29-2 of the Agreement.
3. The ASEAN Secretariat shall provide the necessary technical support and assistance to the ASEAN Insurance Regulators Meeting and to the various ASEAN institutions concerned, in their roles and responsibilities under this Protocol.

Final provisions
1. This Protocol shall be deposited with the Secretary-General of ASEAN, who shall promptly furnish a certified copy thereof to each Contracting Party.
b. This Protocol shall form an integral part of the Agreement.
3. This Protocol shall be subject to ratification or acceptance by the Contracting Parties. The instruments of ratification or acceptance shall be deposited with the Secretary-General of ASEAN, who shall promptly notify each Contracting Party of such deposit.
4. This Protocol shall enter into force when the instruments of ratification or acceptance by the Contracting Parties have been deposited with the Secretary-General of ASEAN. A Contracting Party unable to comply with this Protocol shall be granted a grace period of two years from the date of signature of this Protocol in order to complete the work towards its implementation.
5. Any amendment to the provisions and annexes of this Protocol shall be effected by the consent of all the Contracting Parties.
In witness whereof, the undersigned, being duly authorised by their respective Governments, have signed this Protocol 5 on the ASEAN Scheme on Compulsory Motor Vehicle Insurance.
[Page 40]

Composition and meetings of the Bureau Council
1. The Bureau Council shall consist of one representative from each National Bureau and one representative of the Transit Transport Coordinating Board established in accordance with Article 29-2 of the Agreement.
2. The Bureau Council shall elect a Chairman and a Vice-Chairman from among its members for a fixed term and in accordance with the principle of rotation.
3. The Bureau Council shall meet once a year. Additional meetings may be held at the request of any National Bureau.

The Bureau Council shall have the following functions: a. to determine and approve the form and content of the Blue Card.
b. to prepare its annual budget and to determine the annual contribution to be paid by each National Bureau. c. to coordinate the operations of all the National Bureaux. For that purpose, the Bureau Council shall arrange for an inter-bureau agreement to be signed by all the National Bureaux, which may be amended only by the Bureau Council.
d. to submit recommendations to the authorities concerned, for the purpose of improving the ASEAN Scheme on Compulsory Motor Vehicle Insurance and enhancing measures to prevent road accidents, where necessary through amendments to the laws and regulations in force of the Contracting Parties.
e. to settle disputes between two or more National Bureaux relating to the implementation or interpretation of the provisions of this Protocol.
f. to submit an annual report to the meeting of the ASEAN Insurance Regulators.
